chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), like that.

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq), the source of the narration
key_terms.ابْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ: Ibn Abi Umayr, a prominent narrator of hadith
key_terms.مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ: Like that / Similarly, indicating a reference to a preceding text

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the Mudabbir selling his property according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This brief narration from al-Isfabar utilizes the chain of Hammad ibn al-Halabi to corroborate the permissibility of a Mudabbir selling his property, reinforcing the juristic consensus on the slave's partial autonomy. It highlights the methodological rigor of Shaykh al-Tusi in compiling parallel reports to establish definitive legal precedents within the chapter of manumission.
